summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE, and chronic pelvic fractures was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. Initial evaluation revealed leukopenia, elevated lactate, and diffuse colon wall thickening on CT concerning for colitis versus portal colopathy. She was treated empirically with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. During admission, she developed acute anemia requiring transfusion, transient hypoxia with pulmonary edema managed with diuresis, and mild troponin elevation attributed to demand ischemia. Her mental status fluctuated, consistent with hepatic encephalopathy, managed with lactulose. Imaging confirmed a stable pelvic hematoma without active bleeding and no pulmonary embolism. She improved clinically, resumed oral intake, and was discharged to extended care to complete antibiotic therapy via PICC line, with plans for RFA of recurrent HCC and outpatient stress testing.
